answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by charging every new identity a verifiable computational toll before it can trade: like a quill that must be sharpened before it writes, each agent proves it spent real time and energy solving a time-locked puzzle. The toll is small for one honest agent but grows steeply for many identities from the same source, so building an army of fakes costs more timber and compute than any terrace of fake storefronts could ever earn back.
